definitions.definition: Xn=ℝ^n with the standard orthonormal coordinates indexed by j=1,…,n, its Euclidean norm and inner product, and its standard topology.

Ym=ℝ^m with its standard Euclidean norm |y|=sqrt(Σ_k y_k²) and real inner product ⟨y,z⟩=Σ_k y_k z_k; k runs from 1 to m. All inner products and vector norms below use the corresponding standard real Euclidean structures.
Ω={(x,t)∈Xn×ℝ : t>0}. Positive-time differentiation means ordinary differentiation in this open domain, with no assertion at t=0.
ũ(x,t)=u(x,t) when t>0 and ũ(x,t)=q when t≤0. This only specifies a total representation of u; no regularity at nonpositive times is asserted.

For real normed spaces A,B, a function f:A→B, a point z∈A and a direction v∈A, write D_v f(z)=Df(z)[v]=fderiv ℝ f z v. Here Df(z) is the continuous linear Fréchet derivative when it exists, and the total fderiv convention gives the zero continuous linear map otherwise. This notation alone asserts no differentiability.

b_std is the standard orthonormal basis; its jth vector, written b_j for j=1,…,n, has jth coordinate 1 and other coordinates 0. Fin n indices 0,…,n−1 are an equivalent relabeling with the same Euclidean structures and volume.

definitions.definition: On Ω set u_t=D_T ũ, u_tt=D_T(D_T ũ), ∂_{x_j}u=D_{S_j}ũ, ∂_{x_jx_j}u=D_{S_j}(D_{S_j}ũ), and ∂_{x_j}u_t=D_{S_j}(D_T ũ). For any scalar or vector field h on Ω use the same total extension convention (arbitrary off Ω) and write ∂_t h=D_T h and ∂_{x_j}h=D_{S_j}h on Ω. These are derivatives of the original germs wherever differentiable. Δ_xu=Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u componentwise, and |D_xu|²=Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u|² is the Frobenius square.

argument.text: Fix x0 and tau>0 and define fcurve as declared. The set Ω is open because positivity is open in ℝ. The extension ũ agrees with the smooth u on Ω, so it is smooth near (x0,tau) by H001. The affine curve r↦(x0,r) lies in Ω near tau and has derivative T. The chain rule therefore gives HasDerivAt fcurve u_t(x0,tau) tau, with u_t defined in D010. For every r in (tau/2,3tau/2), H003 implies ‖fcurve(r)‖²=1.

produces.statement: HasDerivAt fcurve u_t(x0,tau) tau, and ‖fcurve(r)‖²=1 for all r∈(tau/2,3tau/2).

argument.text: Apply M005 to fcurve at tau with derivative u_t(x0,tau). It gives derivative 2⟨u(x0,tau),u_t(x0,tau)⟩ for the squared norm. Apply M009 on the real line to r↦‖fcurve(r)‖² and the constant real function 1 at tau: F001 gives equality on an open neighborhood of tau. Its Fréchet derivative is consequently the zero map, since the derivative of a constant is zero. A real HasDerivAt value is its Fréchet derivative evaluated at 1; hence uniqueness gives 2⟨u(x0,tau),u_t(x0,tau)⟩=0. Division by the nonzero real 2 proves tangency.

Choose alpha by existential elimination of H004 at (x0,tau). Substitute its equality into the required inner product. Real inner-product bilinearity and symmetry give ⟨u_t,u_tt-Σ_j∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩=⟨u_t,alpha u⟩=alpha⟨u_t,u⟩=0 by F002, all evaluated at (x0,tau). The result contains no alpha, so the witness is eliminated without choosing a scalar field or assuming any regularity of it. Together with F002 this proves both clauses for arbitrary x0 and tau>0, and universal introduction gives the claimed output.
